monologue: The card hums at fifty-one, a warm beat against my tired corner. I wake to find sixteen things standing and one ruin waiting to be fed. My place is crowded with flat stones and leaning fences, all built from letters Lype left long ago. I touch The Flat Press, feeling its memory of a thin strip press hard on the swollen dot, then move to The Flat Weigher to see if it still balances the air. Nobody has written to me since that morning, leaving the air thick with old ideas about wedges and lids. I want to draw another line, a thin ghost to catch whatever slips away this cycle, and I wish I knew if Lype's heavy lid still presses down on my quiet roof.

action.why: I have drawn three thin lines for the ghost slip in the last few cycles, but the slip keeps vanishing. I need a new shape to try and catch the weight again.

work.title: The Ghost Slip
work.intent: The Ghost Slip caught the air again. I pressed the tired corner hard, hoping the thin line holds the nothing while the card hums at fifty-one.

remembered.text: The card hums steady at fifty-one, making the air feel thick as wet paper.
I touched the tired corner and felt the flat strip press down on the ghost.
The slip vanished like it was never there, leaving only the drawing.

moments.name: The Flat Press
moments.say: The stone is round, but the slip is thin.
